issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts two equalities that are false: (1) sum_i H_{i,l} = |C_l| and (2) sum_i f_i^{(s)} H_{i,l} = |V_s ∩ C_l|. The matrix H is a real-valued eigenvector embedding, not a hard clustering indicator matrix; its entries are not 0/1 cluster-membership values. Therefore the sum of column entries of H has no relation to cluster sizes, and the inner product of f^{(s)} with a column of H does not count group members in a cluster. The claimed exact equivalence between the proportionality condition on the final k-means clusters and the linear constraint F^T H = 0 does not hold.

The constraint itself (from Kleindessner et al.) remains a valid spectral relaxation, but the paper's own proof of its exact equivalence to the cluster-level fairness condition fails.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows

issues.failure_explanation: Two distinct errors combine here. First, Z is an n × (n−h+1) matrix with orthonormal columns (Z^T Z = I), so it is not square and has no two-sided inverse; the assertion Z^T = Z^{-1} is undefined. Second, even setting that aside, the claim that maximizing Tr(Y^T Z^T G Z Y) over Y^T Y = I yields the same optimizer as minimizing Tr(Y^T Z^T G^{-1} Z Y) is false in general. While the top-k eigenvectors of G coincide with the bottom-k eigenvectors of G^{-1} in the full space, this property is lost under projection onto a proper subspace: the top-k eigenvectors of Z^T G Z need not be the bottom-k eigenvectors of Z^T G^{-1} Z. A concrete counterexample (n=3, h=2, k=1, F^T=(1,0,0), G=diag(1,3,1)⊕off-diagonal block) shows the two optimizers are different vectors. The entire Fair-SMW derivation from SMW1 to SMW2 to the SMW formula rests on this false equivalence.

failure_location.quote: Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the false max-to-min conversion under the subspace constraint with a valid derivation (e.g., directly solving the constrained eigensystem via the augmented Lagrangian or penalty method without the G^{-1} substitution), or restrict the claim to settings where Z^T G Z and Z^T G^{-1} Z share eigenvectors (which does not hold in general).
issues.overall_effect: The central mathematical derivation of the Fair-SMW algorithm is invalid. The matrix U = G − GF(F^T G F)^{-1} F^T G computed by the algorithm is not (in general) the object whose top-k eigenvectors solve the constrained maximization max Tr(H^T G H) s.t. H^T H = I, F^T H = 0. Consequently, the algorithm's guarantee that its output eigenvectors approximate the fair spectral clustering solution is unsupported. All downstream results that rely on the SMW-derived U (thm:added-3, thm:added-5, alg:smw-cluster) inherit this defect.
issues.title: False equivalence between max Tr(H^T G H) and min Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) under F^T H = 0
issues.why_classification: The false equivalence is the foundational step of the entire Fair-SMW construction. No local edit or sign correction restores the intended guarantee that the algorithm's eigenvectors solve the constrained maximization. A fundamentally different proof architecture is required to link the fairness constraint to the SMW-modified matrix, and without it the central algorithmic contribution has no theoretical support.

issues.failure_explanation: The augmented Lagrangian L(H,Λ,μ) = ½Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) − Tr(Λ^T F^T H) − (μ/2)‖F^T H‖_F² yields, upon setting Λ=0 and taking the gradient, the subproblem min ½Tr(H^T(G^{-1} − μFF^T)H). The immediately preceding display in the source correctly writes G^{-1} − μFF^T. However, the next labelled equation (SMW3) changes the sign to G^{-1} + μFF^T without any justification. These are different optimization problems with different eigensystems (the +μ version has G^{-1}+μFF^T positive definite; the −μ version need not be). The subsequent SMW inversion and μ→∞ limit are carried out on the +μ matrix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either correct SMW3 to read G^{-1} − μFF^T and re-derive the SMW limit for that matrix (showing the same asymptotic result), or add an explicit justification for replacing the subproblem matrix by G^{-1}+μFF^T (e.g., noting both share the same μ→∞ limit and the latter is PD).
issues.overall_effect: The derivation contains an unjustified sign flip between the subproblem and SMW3. The final asymptotic expression U = G − GF(F^T GF)^{-1}F^T G is in fact the same limit whether one uses +μ or −μ, so the end formula is not affected. However, the intermediate step is mathematically incorrect as written, and the positive-definiteness argument (thm:added-1) that applies to G^{-1}+μFF^T does not apply to the actual subproblem matrix G^{-1}−μFF^T.
issues.title: Sign error: augmented-Lagrangian subproblem gives G^{-1} − μFF^T but SMW3 states G^{-1} + μFF^T
issues.why_classification: The sign error is a local algebraic slip in one displayed equation. The final SMW limit and the resulting matrix U are unchanged. The fix is a one-symbol correction plus a brief justificatory sentence; no new construction or re-derivation is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
then the matrix 
$$U = G_{\text{sym}}-G_{\text{sym}}F(F^T G_{\text{sym}}F)^{-1}F^T G_{\text{sym}}$$ is also a real and symmetric.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that U_sym = G_sym − G_sym F(F^T G_sym F)^{-1} F^T G_sym is symmetric because G_sym is symmetric. However, (G_sym F(F^T G_sym F)^{-1} F^T G_sym)^T = G_sym F^T(F^T G_sym F)^{-1} F^T G_sym, which equals G_sym F(F^T G_sym F)^{-1} F^T G_sym only when F = F^T (i.e., h−1 = 1, so h = 2). For h > 2, F is n × (h−1) with multiple columns, F ≠ F^T in general, and U_sym is not symmetric. The theorem is stated without restricting h, so the proof is invalid for the general case it purports to cover.

failure_location.quote: is also a real and symmetric.

The conclusion may still be true (U_sym could be similar to a symmetric matrix via other arguments), but it is not supported by the given proof. The Fair-SMW algorithm's claim that its eigendecomposition yields real-valued eigenvectors is unproven for multi-group settings.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-3: proof claims U_sym is symmetric, which fails for h > 2
issues.why_classification: The proof's key inference (symmetry of U_sym) is invalid for h > 2, but the conclusion (real eigenvalues) is plausibly true and can be recovered with a contained nontrivial argument (similarity to a symmetric matrix). This does not require new global architecture but does require a new lemma or construction beyond a one-line fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore the eigenvalues of $B=\frac{1}{2}(D^{-1}W+WD^{-1})$ belong in $[-1,1]$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims |x^T D^{-1}W x| / (x^T x) ≤ 1 for all x, implying eigenvalues of B = ½(D^{-1}W + WD^{-1}) lie in [−1,1]. This is false. D^{-1}W is similar to the symmetric A_sym (eigenvalues in [−1,1]), but the symmetric part B = ½(A + A^T) of a non-symmetric matrix A can have eigenvalues whose magnitude exceeds 1 even when A's eigenvalues are in [−1,1]. Concrete counterexample: a star graph K_{1,n−1} with n ≥ 15. For n=15, the extremal Rayleigh quotient of B reaches |λ| ≈ 15/(2√14) ≈ 2.004 > 1, so λ_min(B) < −2, making C = B + 2I indefinite (λ_min(C) < 0). Hence x^T G_rw x = x^T C x < 0 for some x, contradicting the theorem's claim that x^T G_rw x > 0. The 'generalized positive definite' assertion in the theorem statement is false for such graphs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the 'generalized positive definite / x^T G_rw x > 0' claim from the theorem statement. Replace the invalid eigenvalue-bound proof for B with the correct similarity argument: D^{-1}W is similar to A_sym = D^{-1/2}WD^{-1/2}, so D^{-1}W has real eigenvalues in [−1,1], and G_rw = D^{-1}W + 2I has real eigenvalues in [1,3]. Optionally add a sufficient condition (e.g., bounded degree ratio d_max/d_min ≤ c) under which the symmetric part B + 2I is indeed positive definite.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's 'generalized positive definite' claim (x^T G_rw x > 0) is false for graphs with sufficiently skewed degree distributions (e.g., star graphs with n ≥ 15). The proof's eigenvalue bound for B is invalid. However, G_rw = D^{-1}W + 2I does have real eigenvalues in [1,3] (by the similarity to A_sym), so it remains invertible with positive eigenvalues. The algorithmic requirement (G invertible, real eigenvalues) is still met; the false part is the additional 'generalized positive definite' assertion and the proof technique used to establish the bounds.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-4: eigenvalue bound for B = ½(D^{-1}W + WD^{-1}) is invalid; 'generalized positive definite' claim is false
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement contains a false assertion (generalized positive definiteness) that must be removed or restricted, and the proof's central eigenvalue bound is invalid. The repair requires a contained argument (similarity-based eigenvalue bounding) and a modification of the statement, but does not alter the core algorithmic requirement (G_rw invertible with real positive eigenvalues), which remains true.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $D^{-1}$ is an invertible diagonal matrix, it is of full rank, and multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space $ \mathcal{R}(F^T D^{-1}) = \mathcal{R}(F^T) $

issues.failure_explanation: The identity (eq. identity) F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} F(F^T F)^{-1} F^T requires that the row space of F^T D^{-1} be contained in the row space of F^T. The paper justifies this by claiming right-multiplication by the invertible diagonal D^{-1} does not change the row space. This is incorrect: right-multiplying F^T (an (h−1)×n matrix) by D^{-1} scales each column j by 1/d_j, which generally changes the row space. Concretely, row space of F^T D^{-1} = col((F^T D^{-1})^T) = col(D^{-1} F), while row space of F^T = col(F). Since D^{-1}F scales rows of F by different factors, col(D^{-1}F) ≠ col(F) in general. A simple counterexample: F^T = (1,1) (1×2), D^{-1} = diag(1,2). Then F^T D^{-1} = (1,2), and row space of (1,2) ≠ row space of (1,1). The identity fails, and every subsequent step in the proof of thm:added-5 (simplification of P, the similarity argument for U_rw) is built on this false premise.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either (a) establish the correct row-space relationship under specific assumptions on D and F (e.g., F constant on degree-homogeneous groups), or (b) provide an entirely new argument for real eigenvalues of U_rw (e.g., showing U_rw is similar to a symmetric matrix via a non-trivial conjugation that does not require the false identity), or (c) restrict the theorem to the case where D^{-1}F and F span the same subspace and verify this condition holds for the specific F used in the experiments.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of thm:added-5 (real eigenvalues of U_rw) is entirely invalid. The key algebraic simplification of the projector P and the concluding similarity argument U_rw ~ D^{-1/2} W̃ P D^{-1/2} do not follow. Whether U_rw actually has real eigenvalues is therefore unestablished by the source. The RW-Fair-SMW algorithm's theoretical guarantee (that its matrix has a real spectrum amenable to eigensolver computation) is unsupported.
issues.title: Theorem thm:added-5: proof relies on false identity F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} F (F^T F)^{-1} F^T
issues.why_classification: The proof's foundational identity is false and every subsequent step depends on it. However, the conclusion (real eigenvalues of U_rw) may be true and recoverable via a different similarity argument or under additional assumptions on the graph and group structure. The repair requires a new contained argument but does not necessarily alter the algorithm's practical operation (numerical eigensolvers can handle real-spectrum non-symmetric matrices).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Construct the fairness-adjusted matrix $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\mathrm{sym}} - M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}}$

issues.failure_explanation: The SMW derivation in the main text defines P = F(F^T G F)^{-1} F^T G and U = G − GP = G − G F(F^T G F)^{-1} F^T G. The algorithm's step 3 computes U_sym = G_sym − M(F^T M)^{-1}F^T G_sym. For this to equal the SMW matrix G_sym − G_sym F(F^T G_sym F)^{-1}F^T G_sym, one needs M = G_sym F (so F^T M = F^T G_sym F). However, step 2 sets M = G_sym^{-1} F, yielding F^T M = F^T G_sym^{-1} F and U_sym = G_sym − G_sym^{-1} F(F^T G_sym^{-1} F)^{-1} F^T G_sym, which is a different matrix. The algorithm as written does not implement the matrix derived in the theory.

failure_location.quote: Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change step 2 to compute M = G_sym F (removing the inverse). Then F^T M = F^T G_sym F and step 3 correctly constructs U_sym = G_sym − G_sym F(F^T G_sym F)^{-1}F^T G_sym, matching the SMW limit derived in the text.
issues.overall_effect: If implemented as written, the algorithm computes eigenvectors of the wrong matrix (G_sym − G_sym^{-1}F(F^T G_sym^{-1}F)^{-1}F^T G_sym instead of G_sym − G_sym F(F^T G_sym F)^{-1}F^T G_sym). The resulting clustering is not the one supported by the SMW derivation. The label 'projection matrix' for M = G_sym^{-1}F is also misleading, as this matrix is not a projection.

issues.why_classification: The fix is a one-symbol local correction in step 2 of the algorithm (replace G_sym^{-1}F with G_sym F). The surrounding derivation and the intended matrix U are unaffected.
